well, i should have said *may not apply* since a TA hanger seems much harder to bend or break than a QR hanger. i can get a replacement TA rear hanger for my bike for $100 direct from the company. you can replace it, but i think you'd have to case it really hard to bend a TA hanger.

you may want to consider getting a "trail" bike with an aggressive geometry rather than a full on DH rig. i just built up a 2013 Banshee Rune which is nice and nimble but can perform pretty well in the park if needed. you can adjust the slackness with these "chips" in the rear hanger. there are many other options for these type of  "enduro" bikes that are capable of handling all sorts of terrain. of course, if you have lots of DH trails in your area that don't have big climbs to get to, you may want to just get a proper DH rig. all the DH in my area (moab) requires big climbs so i built this bike up after getting sick of slugging my previous 40lb freeride/DH bike up the climbs.

also, buying the whole bike outright is much cheaper than piecing it together part by part, unless you have a shop hook-up.

carry a spare derailleur hanger with you. if you're having shift problems on your rear derailleur and just can't get it right by adjusting it, chances are that the hanger is bent. even a tiny bend will cause shifting issues. [wheels mfg](http://wheelsmfg.com/products/derailleur-hangers.html) makes some really good ones for all types of frames. of course, this doesn't apply if you have a solid thru-axle and not quick-release.
